content:
Suppose I have two repo A and B. Repo A depends on repo B.
Normally, I may organize the directory structure like ~/A and ~/B.
Problem is, if I then do cd ~/A; lake build; cd ~/B; lake build, then in A/.lake, there would be a copy of repo B. This seems rather wasteful in term of build time and disk space.
Suppose (somehow) the git version that repo A depends on is always equal to that checked out in repo B (for example, by always setting repo B's git commit to what repo A requires whenever repo A is updated).
Can I avoid the duplicated build?
The repos are on the same machine? On Linux I would soft-link (ln -s) the directories with the Lean files of repo B inside repo A and add the libs to As lakefile.lean. Any better ideas?

I thought that lake already does use symbolic links when you specify a local path dependency instead of a git dependency.

See https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/wiki/Project-setup:-using-local-development-version-of-a-dependency for a possible setup

specify a local path dependency instead of a git dependency

This is often not the case when I download someone else's repo.

That said, I'd give the wiki page a look.
